body.statement: For every \(m\in\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{reg}}\), the order-two query fiber \(\mathcal F_2(P_m)\subset\mathbb R^2\) contains a smooth one-dimensional curve through \(\theta(m)=(a(m),d(m))^\top\). Restricting the candidates on this curve to \(\alpha_{\mathbb R},\delta_{\mathbb R}\in\mathbb R\), it is locally characterized by \(h=a(m)-\alpha_{\mathbb R}\), \(k=d(m)-\delta_{\mathbb R}\), and \[k(h)=-\frac{U_mh}{V_m+\Sigma_{22,m}h}.\] Both real coordinates vary along the curve. Every sufficiently nearby point is realized by a centered non-Gaussian five-source disturbance law satisfying endpoint independence and independence genericity and inducing the same observed covariance as \(P_m\).
body.justification: This is an information lower bound inside the actual disturbance class, rather than failure of one identification certificate.
body.gap: Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant prove covariance noninjectivity for cyclic Gaussian SEMs but do not construct this projected legal fiber with independent non-Gaussian endpoints.
body.consumer: It tells users that covariance-only sensitivity analysis must vary both outer coefficients, even if the graph and path dependence pattern are accepted.
